title: Beatrix and the Hymn
premise: Xanthe Vasquez, a pest controller with a reputation for debunking the supernatural, is hired to clear an infestation at a farmhouse slated for excavation. Instead of vermin, they find handprints pressed into plaster from within the walls—and beneath the property, a door sealed from the inside. As the harvest moon approaches, Xanthe discovers the Vasquez family name in a ledger of debts owed to something that counts its harvesters by bloodline, and must smuggle their estranged family out of its reach before the count completes. In the end, Xanthe chooses love over duty, taking their family's place in the ledger and sealing themselves behind the door—only to learn that what counts the harvest has been waiting for someone who doesn't believe, because disbelief is the one thing it cannot digest.
about_author: Zephyrine Pemberton is the pen name of a former rural building inspector who spent a decade documenting structural anomalies in houses no one would buy twice. They write horror from a converted chapel in upstate New York, where they keep the original bell rope, just in case.

chapters.title: The Callout
chapters.summary: Xanthe Vasquez arrives at the Holloway farmhouse for a routine pest job, armed with traps, sealant, and a lifetime of practiced skepticism. The client, a nervous excavation foreman named Odile, mentions the crew keeps hearing counting through the floorboards. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: dry professional confidence beginning to crack at the edges.

chapters.title: Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Inspecting the pantry, Xanthe finds small handprints pressed into the plaster—prints made from inside the wall, dusted in flour that hasn't been baked with in years. Odile's crew refuses to enter the east wing. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: unease disguised as methodical note-taking; the first lie Xanthe tells themselves.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Floor
chapters.summary: Tearing up rotting floorboards, Xanthe uncovers a leather ledger listing names across generations—including VASQUEZ, entered three times, each entry annotated with a date: the coming harvest moon. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: cold recognition; the past Xanthe fled has found them first.

chapters.title: Family Business
chapters.summary: Xanthe calls their mother, Marisol, under pretense of a birthday check-in, and learns the family quietly left their last house after 'the counting started.' Marisol begs them not to dig further. POV: Xanthe, intercut with Marisol's phone-side scene. Emotional beat: guilt and old wounds reopening along fault lines of duty.

chapters.title: Sealed from Within
chapters.summary: The excavation crew's backhoe strikes stone: a door set into the earth, bolted shut from the other side, warm to the touch. That night the counting through the floorboards reaches forty-one and stops, expectant. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: collective dread as the workers realize the house was built as a lid.

chapters.title: What the Crew Buried
chapters.summary: Odile confesses the company knew about the anomaly—the site was flagged decades ago and quietly re-permitted. She offers Xanthe hush money. Xanthe refuses and instead asks for the original survey maps. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: complicity exposed; justice outside the law begins with refusing the legal settlement.

chapters.title: The Vasquez Debt
chapters.summary: Following the survey maps to a county archive, Xanthe finds their great-grandfather signed a covenant: protection in exchange for 'a body per count, when the moon is full and low.' The debt transfers down the bloodline. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: horror curdling into fury at ancestors who sold descendants like grain.

chapters.title: Marisol Comes
chapters.summary: Against Xanthe's orders, Marisol arrives at the farmhouse, insisting the family faces the count together or not at all. That night, all three Vasquez names in the ledger darken with fresh ink. POV: Marisol. Emotional beat: fierce, stubborn maternal love arriving exactly when it's least convenient.

chapters.title: The Third Name
chapters.summary: Xanthe realizes the third Vasquez entry isn't them—it's their younger brother Teo, whom no one has heard from in two years. The thing counts what it can find, and it has begun finding him. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: panic reframed as purpose; the skeptic now believes entirely, and hates it.

chapters.title: Rules of the Count
chapters.summary: Researching the covenant's origins, Xanthe interviews a dying archivist who explains the terms: the entity may claim only those present when the count completes at moonrise, unless a Vasquez volunteers to close the ledger. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: grim clarity—a loophole exists, and every version of it costs a life.

chapters.title: Evacuation
chapters.summary: Xanthe attempts to move the whole family out of county before moonrise, but roads loop back to the farmhouse no matter which direction they drive. The property isn't a place; it's a perimeter. POV: Marisol. Emotional beat: claustrophobic despair as geography itself becomes the jailer.

chapters.title: Teo Answers
chapters.summary: Xanthe finally reaches Teo by phone—he's been living three towns over, hearing counting in his own walls. He agrees to come, against everyone's advice, because he won't let his family face it without him. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: fractured family choosing each other over safety.

chapters.title: The Warm Door
chapters.summary: Reunited, the Vasquez family examines the buried door together. Through the stone, faintly, something recites their names like a grace before meals. Xanthe presses a palm flat against the warmth and feels it press back. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: terrible intimacy; the monster knows them better than they know themselves.

chapters.title: Odile's Choice
chapters.summary: Odile returns with her crew to break the door open against all warnings, hoping destroying the threshold voids the covenant. The tools melt. One worker is taken—not killed, but subtracted, leaving only his boots and a new line in the ledger. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: guilt detonating; good intentions feeding the count.

chapters.title: The Volunteer Clause
chapters.summary: Xanthe deciphers the archivist's final notes: a willing Vasquez who enters before moonrise closes the ledger permanently—but the entity keeps what it takes, forever, on the other side of the door. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: quiet resolve forming beneath terror; love against duty reaching its crux.

chapters.title: Arguments at Moonrise Minus Two
chapters.summary: The family fights over who will volunteer. Marisol claims seniority, Teo claims youth, Xanthe claims authorship—they brought this to light. Each secretly plans to go alone. POV: rotating between all three. Emotional beat: heartbreaking competition of self-sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Rises
chapters.summary: The moon crests the treeline early, wrong and swollen. The counting resumes—forty-one, forty-two—and the farmhouse begins folding inward toward the door, rooms rearranging to herd the family home. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: escalating panic as time and space both run out.

chapters.title: Through the Door
chapters.summary: Xanthe breaks free of the folding house, bolts the door open from the outside—the only way it has ever opened willingly—and steps through, speaking their full name into the ledger before Marisol or Teo can follow. The door seals behind them, this time from the outside. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: sacrifice rendered in calm, deliberate detail.

chapters.title: The Other Side
chapters.summary: Beyond the door, Xanthe finds a mirrored farmhouse filled with everyone ever counted—generations of Vasquez kin, patient and pale, including the vanished crewman. The entity appears not as a monster but as an accountant with Xanthe's own face. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: awe and horror fused; identity dissolving at the threshold.

chapters.title: What Disbelief Does
chapters.summary: The accountant explains it harvests belief—it feeds on conviction, on families who pass faith in it down like heirlooms. Xanthe, who never believed, is indigestible. Their refusal to accept the covenant's reality begins unraveling the ledger from within. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: triumphant inversion; the flaw becomes the weapon.

chapters.title: Unwriting the Count
chapters.summary: Xanthe tears the ledger apart page by page while the mirrored house screams, freeing the counted dead to walk out through the opening door. Marisol and Teo hold it open from the farm side as dawn bleaches the fields. POV: alternating Xanthe and Marisol. Emotional beat: cathartic destruction; justice delivered by hand, outside any law.

chapters.title: Beatrix and the Hymn
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the family buries the ledger's ashes and sings the old hymn their great-grandfather used to drown out the counting—reclaimed as a song of survival. Xanthe still hears faint numbers some nights, but now hums over them. The door site is a garden. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; belief chosen freely, in love, at last.
